paper_summary: A review/short study from Moscow Power Engineering Institute on syntactic foams (hollow-microsphere-filled polymer coatings) used as thin-film thermal insulation for heat supply equipment and pipelines. It classifies insulating materials, compares aluminosilicate (fly-ash), solid/hollow glass and thermoplastic polymer microspheres, and reports measured thermal conductivity of one-layer syntactic foam coatings made with de-aerated (rarefied-air-filled) versus gas-filled hollow glass microspheres at 60 C and 100 C. The main finding is that coatings based on de-aerated hollow glass microspheres have roughly an order of magnitude lower thermal conductivity than gas-filled ones, while polymer microspheres are limited to ~90 C service temperature.

extraction_notes: Review-style paper with only one set of the authors' own quantitative measurements (thermal conductivity of one-layer syntactic foam coatings). OCR mangles degree signs: '+500C - +1200C' is the +50 to +120 C range, '600C'=60 C and '1000C'=100 C; temperatures were read accordingly. test_type set to 'other' because the measurement is steady-state thermal conductivity, not a mechanical test. Matrix/binder is never identified (the paper only says 'various binding agents'), so matrix_class='other' and matrix_name=null; process_route='other' since the coating application method is not described. Particle volume/weight fraction is not reported for the tested coatings. Table 1 (materials classification) and Table 3 (microsphere characteristics) contain no composite property data. Table 2 lists properties of conventional insulants (mineral wool, PU foam, foamed concrete, etc.), which are not hollow-particle composites, so no records were made from it. Fig. 1 values were not read off the plot; only the values stated in the text were used. Particle size and density ranges quoted in Sec. 4 are generic literature ranges for microsphere classes, not measurements on the tested coatings, so they were left null and only noted in microstructure_notes.
